claim: For the standard encoding \(S_0\) of binary deterministic sequential transducers, the finite-state complexity satisfies \(C(0^n)\ge 2\sqrt{2n}+4\) for every integer \(n\ge1\), and equality holds exactly when \(n=2a^2\) for an integer \(a\ge1\); in particular, \(C(0^{2a^2})=4a+4\).
integrity: The universal lower bound is proved analytically, not inferred from finite experiments.
The upper bound is an explicit one-state transducer construction.
A related 2011 journal article was not inspected in full; residual literature-overlap risk remains.
scientific_limitations: Exact values are established only for n=2a^2, a>=1.
The complexity for other n and the global asymptotic leading constant are not determined.
The proof depends on the stated S0 transition-output encoding length 2|v|+2.
title: Exact finite-state complexity on a quadratic subsequence
